title: 2002 HMMT February Guts Problem 34
statement: Points \(P\) and \(Q\) are 3 units apart. A circle centered at \(P\) with a radius of \(\sqrt{3}\) units intersects a circle centered at \(Q\) with a radius of 3 units at points \(A\) and \(B\). Find the area of quadrilateral APBQ.

solutions.text: The area is twice the area of triangle \(A P Q\), which is isosceles with side lengths \(3,3, \sqrt{3}\). By Pythagoras, the altitude to the base has length \(\sqrt{3^{2}-(\sqrt{3} / 2)^{2}}=\sqrt{33} / 2\), so the triangle has area \(\frac{\sqrt{99}}{4}\). Double this to get \(\frac{3 \sqrt{11}}{2}\).
